A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same evolving tabular-synthesis research, with the same authors and overlapping methods, datasets, and evaluation tasks. All 27 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v2, including supplementary material, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison despite extensive revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on ten datasets, comparing regularized and vanilla generative models through statistical similarity, TSTR, and augmentation evaluations. Tables 3–15 and supplementary Figures 3–15 contain empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on twenty datasets, including diffusion models, Bayesian-optimization comparisons, joint ablations, and computational timings in Tables 5–9 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: v1 correlates paired real/generated samples and compares normalized column sums. v2 instead matches pairwise feature correlations and multiple statistical moments through different losses (Equations 1–8). It also adds a diffusion-specific regularizer and IORBO, which repeatedly reranks evaluated configurations and refits the optimizer. These substantially change training and optimization procedures.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from ten to twenty reported datasets, adding datasets such as Abalone, Cardio, Gesture, Insurance, and Diabetes-ML while removing CoverType, Intrusion, and MNIST28. Classification, regression, TSTR, and augmentation remain, but coverage now includes much smaller datasets while losing the earlier largest and highest-dimensional evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 retains the eight earlier generative-model variants and adds evaluated TabDDPM-MLP and TabDDPM-ResNet baselines (Table 6). It also introduces actual comparisons against SBO-Mean and SBO-Median for the new IORBO method (Tables 8–9). These materially expand the comparator set beyond v1.

E3.justification: v1 uses fixed learning rates, batch sizes, 3,000 training epochs, and default downstream-model settings. v2 introduces Bayesian tuning, five-fold cross-validation for downstream models, and 30-trial search spaces covering architectures, batch sizes, and 100–2,000 epochs (Appendix A). Win-rate evaluation is added, and OPTIMAL/LAST checkpoint comparisons disappear. The 80/20 split remains.

E4.justification: v1 examines four binary correlation/mean-loss configurations and OPTIMAL versus LAST models. v2 introduces a substantial joint ablation crossing vanilla, correlation, distribution, and combined losses with SBO/IORBO under mean and median aggregation (Table 9). Figure 6 additionally investigates optimization overhead across different metric counts.

E5.justification: v1 reports Friedman/Nemenyi significance categories and descriptive distributions without bootstrap standard errors. v2 retains those significance tests and adds standard errors estimated from 1,000 bootstrap rounds throughout Tables 5–9. This introduces a substantive uncertainty-estimation practice; it does not establish additional independent training runs.

E6.justification: Under revised methods and settings, v2 reports a TSTR win rate of 0.611 (SE 0.007) and IORBO win rates of 0.591/0.561 against SBO-Mean/Median. CTAB-GAN's TSTR comparison changes from significantly positive in v1 Table 4 to significantly negative in v2 Table 6; TVAE changes from negative to nonsignificant. These are different-setting findings. v1's detailed supplementary results are removed.

T1.justification: v1 defines its losses but provides no comparable formal guarantees. v2 substantially revises the mathematical definitions and adds Section 4, including sub-Gaussian and moment-matching assumptions, stability Propositions 4.2 and 4.4 with proofs, and an empirical-moment consistency claim in Remark 4.5.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes a GAN-focused correlation/mean regularizer and benchmarking framework, acknowledging limited VAE effectiveness. v2 claims a unified training, tuning, and evaluation framework, successful regularization across GANs, VAEs, and diffusion models, theoretical stability and consistency, and superior hyperparameter selection through IORBO. This substantially broadens the central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 shifts architecture-specific caution from VAEs to CTAB-GAN and newly interprets correlation loss as the dominant component, with distribution loss providing complementary robustness. It adds substantive boundaries concerning unmeasured continuous-categorical dependencies, application to embeddings rather than raw images/text, and computational constraints on million-row evaluations.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-repository address, Hyperopt/TPE implementation information, and Appendix A's detailed ML and generative-model search spaces and trial budgets. Remark 4.1 newly documents treating estimated statistics as constants during differentiation. These considerably expand reproducibility documentation, although TabDDPM search settings remain delegated to a cited paper rather than supplied locally.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through comparisons with CORAL, heterogeneous-data VAEs/VAEM, hierarchical imputation methods, and Bayesian optimization/TPE. The introduction also discusses diffusion/flow/tree approaches. This reframes the work around statistical regularization and integrated optimization, beyond v1's predominantly GAN and medical-data discussion.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around a unified modeling lifecycle. Methods are reorganized into separate loss, optimization, evaluation, tuning, statistical-testing, and framework subsections. The results narrative is substantially revised, and the supplementary-results section is replaced by a hyperparameter-search appendix.

P2.justification: v2 removes the standard-GAN schematic and v1's supplementary metric-distribution plots, redraws the evaluation/framework diagrams, and adds optimization diagrams, side-by-side algorithms, toy-example tables, and a timing figure. Result tables replace OPTIMAL/LAST columns with significance and win-rate/error columns, while the appendix introduces extensive search-space tables.

improvement.justification: v2 adds valuable model coverage, joint ablations, uncertainty estimates, and tuning documentation, but removes v1's granular supplementary results. Its new central guarantees also have unresolved mathematical gaps: Proposition 4.2 differentiates a single correlation pair while claiming a bound for the summed loss, and Remark 4.5 assigns synthetic moments real-distribution limits without establishing their equality. These substantive gains and weaknesses in supporting stronger claims prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
